summary.headline: Havells' Q4 FY26 was modest: channel stocking for cooling hit by a mild start to summer, while cost inflation from the West Asia war drove calibrated price hikes of 5-20%.
summary.overview: Management described a modest Q4 with cooling-product channel stocking hit by a milder start to the season, while industrial and infrastructure-linked categories stayed strong and consumer categories saw cautious trade sentiment. Cables and wires volume grew 6% YoY, with value up 14%, helped by copper and aluminium inventory gains and an approximately 8% blended price increase. Margins held except at Lloyd, which was hit by lower revenue, and a Rs 283 crore fair-value gain on the Goldi Solar investment was booked in other income. Management declined to give FY27 volume or revenue guidance, citing the uncertain war and inflation backdrop.

segments.name: Cables and Wires
segments.commentary: Volume grew 6% YoY, with industrial cables growing much faster than domestic wires, which were flat to slightly down after destocking in the first half of Q4 against a high base. Margins rose sharply, partly from copper and aluminium inventory gains and year-end adjustments. New capacity is still running at high utilisation, and the full planned capacity is expected by end-FY26 or Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Revenue was broadly flat YoY while contribution margin rose to 37%, which management attributed to year-end releases. The long-term margin range is 30-32%, and ASP decline has stabilised.

segments.name: Lloyd (cooling and appliances)
segments.commentary: Q4 was hit by lower revenue from a delayed summer and channel inventory build; the first half of April was also slow. Price hikes of 8-15% by AC type are being implemented to pass on post-war cost increases. A new refrigerator plant at Ghiloth was commissioned in Q4.

segments.name: Fans and ECD
segments.commentary: Fans degrew in value for the full year, with Q4 hit by BEE-norm pre-stocking in Q3 and seasonality. Management expects better volumes in Q1 FY27 on a low base.

segments.name: Other (Solar)
segments.commentary: Other segment grew about 48% YoY, mainly from solar, and its EBIT margin expanded. Management called solar a sunrise industry and said margins should keep improving with operating leverage, but gave no target.

segments.name: Switchgear
segments.commentary: Contribution margin fell below the roughly 38% level because price increases lagged cost increases. Management said it is striving to return to 38% while balancing market share.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 volume or revenue growth guidance; management said it is too early given month-to-month uncertainty from the war and inflation.
Calibrated price hikes are underway across all categories, ranging from 5% to 20% by product range, with Lloyd AC hikes at 8-15%.
Management expects operating leverage in FY27, with revenue growth ahead of expense growth except advertising and promotion, which will rise by choice.
Management reiterated a medium-term EBITDA margin improvement of over 2 percentage points.
Channel inventory for Lloyd is expected to normalise by the end of April 2026 as the summer picks up in the south and west and reaches the north.
Major FY27-28 capex goes to cables and wires, about Rs 800 crore this year, plus a new R&D centre over the next 2-2.5 years. No major new Lloyd capex is planned.
capex_capacity: Cables and wires: new capacity is running at high utilisation, and the full planned capacity is expected by end-FY26 or Q1 FY27. About Rs 800 crore is budgeted this year, mainly for cables and wires.
Lloyd: a new refrigerator plant at Ghiloth was commissioned in Q4 FY26, with a refreshed product portfolio launched. No major new Lloyd capex is planned.
Solar: capacity is being built through the Goldi Solar investment (Rs 600 crore this year), and management plans to widen the renewable product range.
Underground cables are an under-invested area that the company is now investing in.
A new R&D centre will absorb a large share of capex over the next 2-2.5 years.
demand_pricing: Cooling demand was delayed by a mild start to the season. The first half of April was slow, but south and west have started well and the north is following.
Industrial and infrastructure-linked categories remained strong, while consumer categories saw cautious trade sentiment because of higher costs from West Asia disruptions.
Pricing: management said it had not seen price escalation this steep across categories in recent memory. Price increases are calibrated, and management is balancing pass-through against market share.
Pre-buying happened in March ahead of price hikes, especially in cooling products, which management said was accentuated by the price increases.
Copper prices dipped in February and then rose after the war began. Management said the entire increase seen is post-war.

Management said the company is retaining market share in all categories and denied losing share in any category. It said fans, ACs and air coolers degrew for the full year, and it does not disclose product-wise volumes.
Management said a large cement company's entry into housing wires is expected to bring consolidation and some reallocation between the unorganised and organised segments.
B2C to B2B mix has stayed at about 75:25 to 70:30, and management does not expect a meaningful shift.

qa_highlights.question: Had cables and wires volumes declined despite the 14% value growth, and was this destocking or weak end-demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume grew 6% YoY. Industrial cables grew much faster than domestic wires, which were flat. Wires saw destocking in the first half of Q4 against a high base from Q4 FY25 channel stocking.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lighting margins spike to 37% when revenue was flat, and does the margin normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the spike to year-end releases of dealer incentives and adjustments. The long-term average is 30-32%, and ASP decline has stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Lloyd channel inventory and sell-in/sell-out trends?
qa_highlights.answer: The first half of April was slow, and some channel inventory built up. Management expects normalised channel inventory by the end of April as summer picks up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and revenue outlook, including a double-digit volume and price-led value growth scenario?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, saying it is difficult to predict amid the war and inflation. It said price hikes could affect demand if they are too steep.

qa_highlights.question: Will price hikes fully offset raw-material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is striving to pass on costs but must also compete and retain market share, so it will be a balancing act.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase has been taken for Lloyd and what more is needed to restore double-digit contribution margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a work in progress. Price increases of 8-15% depending on the AC type are being passed on, with post-war cost increases now flowing through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the weighted average price increase above 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said price increases range from 5% to 20% across product ranges, and it did not confirm a weighted average.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 48% growth in the Other segment, and will margins keep expanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of the Other growth came from solar, which benefited from capacity additions and tight supply. Management expects growth and margin improvement to continue but gave no target.

qa_highlights.question: How much cables and wires price increase was taken, and what was the volume-price split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed 6% volume growth and 14% value growth, implying a blended price increase of about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: How will fixed costs and capex change in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Some investment will continue across segments in a balanced way. The company aims for revenue growth to outpace expense growth, except advertising and promotion, which will rise by choice.

risks_watch: Demand elasticity: steep price hikes across categories could slow consumer offtake, and management said it is tracking this closely.
Raw-material and forex inflation from the West Asia conflict, plus gas-supply disruptions that hit production, with only partial pass-through so far.
Lloyd returns: about Rs 4,000 crore of capital is deployed with barely any profitability, and management's turnaround depends on brand building and operating leverage.
Switchgear margin recovery toward 38% depends on price catch-up without losing share.
New entrants in housing wires, including a large cement company, could add pricing pressure.
Fans and cooling Q1 FY27 volumes, which depend on the summer and monsoon, after BEE-norm stocking in Q3 FY26.
Cables and wires margins may have been boosted by one-off inventory gains and year-end adjustments, so the quarter's margin is not a run rate.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near-term numbers: management declined to give FY27 volume or revenue guidance and repeatedly said it is too early to call. It was more confident on the long-term plan (brand, innovation, distribution, medium-term margin improvement of over 2 points) and on the cables and solar growth runways.
key_quotes: Modest overall performance for the quarter as channel stocking for cooling products was impacted by milder start to season.
So, overall volumes were down during the quarter.
Yes, we are striving towards that. As I said, in certain cases, the cost increases are so high that there was a lag in passing on the entire price increase.

So our focus in Lloyd will continue to be towards bringing out better products through innovation, which means improving image through brand building and innovation for a better margin and utilize the capacities that have been created for better operating leverage.

adds.what: New cables and wires capacity (planned full capacity; Rs 800 crore budgeted this year mainly for cables and wires)
Lloyd new refrigerator plant at Ghiloth

growth.why: No FY27 volume or revenue guidance was given, citing war and inflation uncertainty; management expects operating leverage and a medium-term EBITDA margin gain of over 2 points, backed partly by new cables capacity (full capacity by end-FY26/Q1 FY27) and calibrated 5-20% price hikes.
